meta.topic: Mobile (and desktop) performance regression from this session's hero scene + Work filmstrip work - Gene asked whether it's laggy and wants a plan, explicitly NOT to implement yet ('先不急著改')
meta.method: npm run build + vite preview (production build, port 4173) + npx lighthouse@12.8.2 --preset=perf, throttling-method=simulate, both mobile and desktop form factors. Compared against the pre-session baseline already recorded in site-audit-2026-09-15.json.measurements.lighthouse.

after_2026-09-16.caveat: Not a perfectly apples-to-apples run (throttling method/version may differ slightly from the original audit's Lighthouse 13 run), but the absolute numbers and the diagnostic breakdown below are real, from this build, and tell a clear story on their own regardless of the exact delta vs the old baseline.

measurements.verdict: Confirmed regression, and it is NOT mobile-specific - desktop dropped from 99 to 57, proportionally worse than mobile's 81->72. This is a genuine amount of main-thread work, not just mobile CPU throttling exposing something that was always marginal.

diagnostics.lcpElement: Changed from the portrait image (pre-session) to the tagline paragraph ('I build the tooling, backend services...') - the LARGEST content on the page now takes 5.1-5.2s to paint because something is delaying even plain text rendering, not because of image weight.
diagnostics.longTasksBreakdown: Script Evaluation 1430ms, Other 784ms, Style & Layout 311ms, Rendering 193ms (mainthread-work-breakdown audit, mobile run) - script evaluation alone is more than double every other category combined.
diagnostics.renderBlocking: Down to a trivial 1.7KB inline CSS chunk (153ms) - Google Fonts is NO LONGER the render-blocking culprit it was in the original audit, so that finding is stale/already fixed and not the current bottleneck.
diagnostics.conclusion: The ~1.4s of script-evaluation long-task time lines up exactly with this session's addition: OrbitalSystem's entire WebGL scene setup (renderer creation, 6 orbit-line geometries at 256 segments each, 6 sphere meshes at 40x40 segments with MeshStandardMaterial, texture load + canvas masking for the portrait, shader compilation for the custom star/orbit shaders) runs as ONE synchronous block inside a single useEffect. That block is bulldozing straight through the main thread the moment it fires (via requestIdleCallback after first paint), and text painting - which should be nearly free - gets queued behind it.

plan.name: Break up OrbitalSystem's synchronous setup so it stops blocking the main thread
plan.why: This is the one change most directly responsible for the LCP/TTI regression per the diagnostics above - not a guess, the long-task breakdown points straight at script evaluation timed right after the idle-callback trigger.
plan.how: Split the current single useEffect into staged work: renderer + camera + lights first (cheap), THEN yield a frame (requestAnimationFrame or a 0ms setTimeout) before building the 6 orbit geometries, THEN yield again before the star field, THEN the portrait texture load (already async via TextureLoader's callback, that part is fine). Each yield lets the browser paint/respond to input between chunks instead of one uninterrupted block.

result.implementation: Split the single synchronous useEffect into: sync Stage A (renderer/camera/scene/fog/root groups/corona/portrait sprite/lights), then an async IIFE with a yieldToMain() (requestIdleCallback w/ 50ms timeout fallback, falls back to setTimeout(0)) between Stage B (orbit lines + planets) and Stage C (star field). renderer.compile(scene, camera) called after each stage. Observer/listener wiring + start() deferred until all stages complete. Cleanup handles both full-teardown and mid-setup-cancellation via cancelled/wired flags.
result.visualRegression: None - screenshots before/after are pixel-identical, confirmed by Gene.
result.measurementMethod: npm run build + vite preview (port 4173) + lighthouse@12.8.2, mobile form factor. IMPORTANT: switched to --throttling-method=devtools (real CPU/network throttling during recording) instead of the default simulate (post-hoc mathematical estimate) because simulate showed no change at all (0.72->0.70, likely too coarse to register short real-world yields as paint opportunities). devtools is the faithful signal for a main-thread-yielding fix. Same exact build isolated by git stash push -- src/components/OrbitalSystem.tsx for the pre-P1 baseline, git stash pop to restore.
result.verdict: Real, confirmed improvement. TBT (the metric that best tracks perceived jank/input-responsiveness) dropped 240ms->80ms, a 67% reduction. Perf score 0.68->0.73. Script Evaluation long-task time down ~234ms. LCP/FCP/Speed Index only marginally better since P1 doesn't reduce total work, just unblocks the thread during it. TTI unchanged - likely gated by other costs (React/MUI mount, below-fold section code) not yet touched, which is exactly what P3 targets.

plan.name: Cut the WebGL scene's actual render cost on mobile
plan.why: Even once setup is non-blocking, the STEADY-STATE per-frame cost (what Gene calls 卡頓/stutter while scrolling or idling on the hero) is still driven by these settings.
plan.how: (a) antialias:true contradicts powerPreference:'low-power' and is one of the more expensive WebGL flags on mobile GPUs - disable it below the 900px/isSmall breakpoint, the scene is already stylised/blurred so the visual loss is minimal. (b) Cap devicePixelRatio at 1.5 instead of 2 on small hosts. (c) Drop sphere segments 40x40 -> ~20x20 and orbit line segments 256 -> ~96 on mobile via the existing isSmall check - both already have a mobile branch for particle/star counts, this extends the same pattern.

result.implementation: Gene vetoed disabling antialias (wants to keep visual quality), so only (b) and (c) landed: devicePixelRatio capped at 1.5 (was 2) below 900px width, sphere segments 40x40->20x20, orbit line segments 256->96, both gated on the same isSmall = window.innerWidth < 900 check (re-evaluated on every effect rerun, which already happens on a mobile/desktop tuning-profile swap).
result.visualRegression: None at either breakpoint, confirmed via screenshot at 390x844 and 1440x900.
result.measurementMethod: Same lighthouse@12.8.2 --throttling-method=devtools mobile method as P1, isolated via git stash push/pop on OrbitalSystem.tsx.
result.verdict: Flat on Lighthouse's load-time score, as expected and explained to Gene up front: this item targets STEADY-STATE per-frame render cost (scroll/idle smoothness), not initial load, which Lighthouse's audit doesn't measure. Math-based expected win: DPR 3->1.5 is ~4x fewer pixels shaded, sphere segments 40x40->20x20 is ~4x fewer triangles per planet (x6 planets), orbit segments 256->96 is ~2.7x fewer vertices per orbit (x6 orbits). Gene confirmed '還可以' (decent/OK) after testing on his real phone via the deployed push - accepted without further tuning.
result.regressionFoundLater: During WF-round testing, Gene noticed his own portrait looking softer on his phone. The DPR cap was renderer-wide, and the portrait Sprite is drawn inside that same WebGL canvas (not a separate DOM ), so capping to 1.5 downscaled the portrait along with the fogged/blurred orbit furniture the cap was actually aimed at. Reverted the DPR part of P2 back to capping at 2 on all breakpoints (commit a386df6) - a face is scrutinised for sharpness in a way decorative elements aren't. The segment-count reduction (sphere/orbit-line triangle counts) is untouched, since that doesn't touch the portrait at all.

plan.name: Code-split the below-the-fold sections the same way TravelSection already is
plan.why: The main index chunk is 210KB gzip and, per the original audit, already had an 'unused-javascript ~81KiB' finding before this session added more section code (About's flip cards, the Work filmstrip's StageCard/Filmstrip logic, the hero button/typewriter logic). Everything below the fold currently ships in the same eagerly-loaded bundle as the hero.
plan.how: React.lazy() + the same IntersectionObserver-gated placeholder pattern already used for DeferredTravelSection, applied to ExperienceSection, ProjectsSection and ContactSection (About probably stays eager since it's usually the first scroll target). Each becomes its own chunk, loaded just before it scrolls into view.
plan.effort: ~1 day (mostly placeholder/height-reservation work to avoid layout shift, CLS is currently a perfect 0 and must stay that way)

plan.name: Reconsider running two independent animation loops in the hero at once
plan.why: ParticleNetwork (2D canvas, O(n^2) pairwise distance checks for repulsion + connections every frame) and OrbitalSystem (WebGL) both run continuously whenever the hero is in view. Each is individually reasonable-ish now (particle count is density-scaled, WebGL work will shrink after P1/P2), but two independent per-frame loops is still double the scheduling/context-switch overhead of one.
plan.how: Lowest-effort option: nothing structural, just confirm after P1-P3 land whether steady-state frame time is still a problem before touching this - may not be worth the complexity of merging them. If it still is, consider drawing the starfield INTO the WebGL canvas as additional Points (removes the 2D canvas + its own rAF loop entirely) instead of a separate DOM canvas.
plan.effort: ~1 day IF pursued; recommend measuring first, this may turn out unnecessary

plan.name: Adaptive fallback for genuinely low-end or data-saver devices
plan.why: Gene's point about 'strong personal sites don't feel laggy even with rich visuals' - the sites that pull this off usually don't run a full 3D scene unconditionally for every visitor, they gate it. Right now every mobile visitor gets the same WebGL scene regardless of device class or a saveData preference.
plan.how: Check navigator.connection?.saveData and/or navigator.hardwareConcurrency / deviceMemory (where available) once, at mount; below a threshold, skip OrbitalSystem entirely and keep the plain photo + dashed ring (the pre-scene hero), which is still a perfectly good fallback since it's what shipped before this session.

plan.priority: discovered mid-session, not in original P1-P5
plan.name: Work section filmstrip: arrow-tap slide animation is janky on mobile
plan.why: Gene reported after confirming P1/P2 on his phone: tapping the next/prev arrow in the Work filmstrip to slide to the next card feels janky. This is the open question flagged back in this doc's openQuestions ('should StageCard's filmstrip get a similar look now that Work isn't part of this measurement pass') - confirmed yes, it's a real second hot spot.
plan.how: Root-caused to two things in ProjectsSection.tsx: (1) updateScroll() re-queried all cards' offsetLeft on every native 'scroll' event during the smooth-scroll animation, unthrottled - fixed with a requestAnimationFrame coalesce (zero visual impact, kept). (2) The actual dominant cost: backdrop-filter (blur(22px) on the card body, blur(10px) on the org/year pills) is expensive to composite on mobile GPUs, and several cards animate transform/opacity/filter simultaneously during the slide.

result.attemptedAndReverted: First tried toggling backdrop-filter off during the scroll (via a data-scrolling attribute, restored ~120ms after scroll settles) to keep the glass look at rest. Measured WORSE: toggling forces the browser to tear down/rebuild the GPU compositing layer at the moment it flips, which cost more than leaving it on - worst-case frame gap went from ~400ms to ~1400ms in one measurement. Reverted this approach entirely - a real lesson, not just a nitpick: don't dynamically toggle backdrop-filter as a perf fix.
result.implementation: (a) rAF-throttled updateScroll (kept, no visual impact). (b) Static removal below 900px: backdropFilter/WebkitBackdropFilter set to 'none' via sx breakpoint object on both the card body and the org/year pills, background color raised to near-opaque (rgba(11,15,24,0.92) card / rgba(7,9,15,0.82) pills) to compensate for the lost blur so contrast against busy backgrounds doesn't suffer. Desktop (>=900px) keeps the original blur/glass look unchanged.
result.visualRegression: None obvious in screenshots at 390x844 - the near-opaque background reads almost the same as the blurred version at a glance. Desktop confirmed unchanged (still has the glass blur, e.g. neighbouring card visibly blurred behind the active one).
result.measurementLimitation: Could not get a reliable local before/after number for this one, unlike P1/P2. Two methods tried, both failed to be a faithful proxy: (1) headless Chrome forced to software-render via --use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader (the flag used for the WebGL hero work) produced wildly noisy rAF frame-gap data (avg swung 94ms->262ms run to run on the IDENTICAL build) - not trustworthy. (2) Headless Chrome with real macOS GPU + CDP 4x CPU throttle gave clean, low-noise data (~18ms avg frame time, ~60fps) but showed almost no difference before/after (66.7ms worst either way) - because CDP CPU throttling doesn't throttle GPU compositing at all, and a MacBook GPU is far more capable than a phone GPU, so this environment can't reproduce phone-specific backdrop-filter cost either. backdrop-filter being expensive on mobile GPUs specifically (vs. desktop) is a well-documented pattern independent of this session's measurements.
result.verdict: Implemented and pushed on the strength of the well-documented mobile backdrop-filter cost pattern + no visual regression, not a locally-measured number - explicitly flagged this gap to Gene before pushing. Needs his real-phone confirmation (same workflow as P1/P2: push, he tests, reports back) rather than a Lighthouse/Puppeteer number this time.

plan.priority: discovered mid-session, not in original P1-P5
plan.name: Round 2: Work filmstrip still janky after WF1, plus Experience accordion jank
plan.why: Gene tested WF1 on his phone: filmstrip is '好一點' (a bit better) but '還是挺卡' (still pretty janky). Separately reported Experience section (collapse one entry, expand another) is also janky.
plan.how: Experience: MUI Accordion/Collapse animates height via JS-measured scrollHeight + explicit pixel transition, forcing layout every frame - classic anti-pattern, unrelated to anything from WF1/P1/P2. Work filmstrip round 2: the breathing accent-ring glow ran as a Framer JS animate={} loop (repeat: Infinity) on all 11 cards unconditionally regardless of visibility - wasted main-thread work. The ambient-glow layer's blur(48px) on the card's own screenshot is the same GPU-cost category as the backdrop-filter already removed in WF1, just not touched yet.

result.implementation: Experience (mobile only): replaced <Accordion>/<AccordionSummary>/<AccordionDetails> with a plain button header + Box using display:grid, gridTemplateRows: expanded?'1fr':'0fr', transition:'grid-template-rows 0.3s ease', inner Box with overflow:hidden - no JS height measurement, browser interpolates the CSS grid track natively. Work: (a) breathing ring's Framer animate={opacity:[0.55,1,0.55], repeat:Infinity} replaced with an emotion keyframes() CSS animation, same values/timing, respects reducedMotion. (b) ambient glow blur radius reduced from blur(48px) to blur(20px) below the md breakpoint (useMediaQuery(theme.breakpoints.down('md')) added to StageCard), grayscale/brightness coverflow filter and the 11-cards-always-mounted structure both left alone per Gene's confirmation not to touch the core visual design without discussing further.
result.visualRegression: None observed in screenshots (collapsed/expanded Experience states, Work card ring glow) at 390x844.
result.measurementLimitation: Same local-measurement gap as WF1 - no faithful way to reproduce phone-specific GPU/layout-thrash cost in this environment. Shipped on the technical merits (height-animation-forces-layout and idle-animation-still-runs are textbook, uncontroversial performance issues, not judgment calls) plus visual-regression screenshots, not a measured number.
result.verdict: Pending Gene's real-phone re-test. Two candidates flagged but NOT implemented (his call, matches the antialias/DPR pattern of not silently changing core visual design): further reducing/removing the grayscale+brightness coverflow filter, and virtualizing the filmstrip so only cards near the viewport mount their full useScroll/useTransform chain instead of all 11 always running.

plan.priority: discovered mid-session, not in original P1-P5
plan.name: Round 3: real on-device profiling breaks the guessing loop
plan.why: WF2 still didn't fix it - Gene reported both Work and Experience 'still a bit janky' after a fresh reload (ruled out stale cache: confirmed no service worker/PWA caching exists in this codebase, vercel.json has no custom cache rules). Rounds WF1/WF2 were reasonable-but-unverified guesses since local Lighthouse/Puppeteer measurement couldn't reproduce phone-specific GPU cost (documented in WF1). Pivoted to getting a REAL trace instead of guessing further: walked Gene through connecting his iPhone to his Mac via USB, enabling Web Inspector (Settings > Safari > Advanced), and recording a Timelines capture in Safari's Web Inspector while performing the janky interaction on the actual phone.
plan.how: Gene shared a screenshot of the Web Inspector Timelines recording. It showed 'Recalculate Style' and 'Layout' as the dominant, near-continuous activity across the whole ~8s window - not just during the touch/scroll events (which only clustered around 2-3.5s and 4.5-5.5s) but well past where they ended. CPU never exceeded 38.7%, ruling out simple CPU saturation. This pointed at forced synchronous layout rather than raw script cost. Root cause found in Filmstrip's nearestIndex(): it read offsetLeft/offsetWidth off every one of the N card elements on every scroll frame (the rAF-throttled handler from WF1) to find which card is centred - a DOM geometry READ running in a separate rAF callback from the one Framer Motion uses internally to WRITE each card's transform/filter style. Reading layout-dependent geometry interleaved with another callback writing style to those same elements is the textbook forced-synchronous-layout / layout-thrashing pattern, firing every frame of every slide.
plan.effort: ~0.25 day once the real cause was known (the profiling/troubleshooting took longer than the fix)

result.implementation: Cards are uniform width with scroll-snap-align: center, so the active index is recoverable from scrollLeft alone (a cheap, non-layout-forcing read) once the fixed pixel spacing between card centres is known. Added measureStep() which reads offsetLeft off just the first two cards ONCE on mount and on ResizeObserver fire (not every scroll frame) to get that spacing; nearestIndex() now does Math.round(scrollLeft / step) instead of querying and reading all N cards' geometry every frame.
result.verification: No visual/behavioural change expected or observed - verified programmatically (not just by eye) that the active-card counter still advances/retreats correctly and clamps at both ends through 5x next-clicks then 6x prev-clicks (01/11 -> 06/11 -> 01/11, held at the floor on the 6th prev click).
result.measurementLimitation: Still no local before/after number - same gap as WF1/WF2 - but this fix is grounded in an actual on-device trace for the first time in this investigation, not a plausible-pattern guess.
result.verdict: Pending Gene's re-test, ideally with the SAME Web Inspector Timelines method that found this - that would give an actual before/after comparison on real hardware, the first reliable one in this whole mobile-perf investigation. Lesson for future rounds: ask for a real device trace much earlier once 1-2 rounds of guess-and-check don't fully resolve a reported jank, rather than continuing to guess against known-expensive-CSS-pattern heuristics with no way to verify locally.
result.misattributionFound: Gene confirmed afterwards that the Web Inspector recording analysed here was actually of the EXPERIENCE section (scrolling the page + tapping accordion items), not the Work filmstrip - I misread which interaction it captured. The filmstrip fix above (nearestIndex via scrollLeft math) is still a real, independently-justified fix and Gene confirmed Work did get smoother from it, but it was NOT what that specific trace showed. See WF4 for the correctly-attributed root cause.

plan.priority: discovered mid-session, not in original P1-P5
plan.name: Round 4: the real Experience-jank cause, found via correctly-attributed trace + subagent code search
plan.why: After WF3 shipped, Gene reported Work did get smoother but Experience was still exactly as janky, and separately noticed his own portrait looking softer on his phone, and 1-2 mid-session page reloads back to the top. Re-examining WF3's Web Inspector trace with Gene's correction (it was Experience, not Work) reopened the question of what's actually forcing layout continuously for ~8s while only 2 short touch/scroll bursts occurred.
plan.how: Dispatched a codebase-search subagent to look for any OTHER scroll-linked or continuously-running code that reads layout geometry, since ExperienceSection.tsx's own accordion (already fixed in WF2) wasn't explaining a trace with NO touch/scroll for the last several seconds. Found two: OrbitalSystem.tsx's tick() loop called syncAnchor() (2x getBoundingClientRect()) unconditionally every 20 frames (~3x/sec) for as long as ANY sliver of the hero canvas was in the viewport - including the intentional 'bleed' area (90-200px) extending past the Hero section's own boundary, per HeroSection.tsx's bleedSx. This loop runs completely independent of scroll/touch, decoupled from the actual Experience-section interaction, which explains why the trace's Layout/Recalculate-Style activity outlasted the touch gesture - it was a separate always-on background poll, not anything caused by the accordion itself. ParticleNetwork.tsx's draw() had the same category of bug at smaller scale: canvas.offsetWidth/offsetHeight read directly inside the per-particle boundary-check loop, up to ~100 reads/frame.

result.implementation: OrbitalSystem: removed the unconditional 20-frame poll; syncAnchor() now runs only on actual scroll (rAF-throttled, listener attached to the app's real nested scroll container found via findScrollParent(), since it's a Box with overflowY:auto in App.tsx, not window) and resize, plus a 1.5s post-mount window to track the portrait's own scale-in entrance animation (HeroSection: 0.8s duration + 0.3s delay). ParticleNetwork: cached canvas width/height from the existing ResizeObserver measurement (boundsW/boundsH) instead of re-reading offsetWidth/offsetHeight inside the animation loop.
result.sameSessionRegression: Separately, Gene noticed his own portrait looking softer on his phone - traced to P2's mobile DPR cap (1.5 instead of 2), since the portrait Sprite renders inside the same WebGL canvas as the rest of the scene, not as a separate DOM . Reverted (commit a386df6, recorded under P2's result) before this round shipped.
result.visualRegression: None observed: portrait/corona/sun alignment confirmed via screenshot both at rest and after scrolling the actual nested scroll container 250px (not window.scrollTo, which doesn't affect this app).
result.measurementLimitation: Same gap as WF1-WF3 - no local reproduction of phone GPU/layout cost - but grounded in a correctly-attributed real trace plus concrete code evidence (an always-on 3x/sec polling loop scoped to hero visibility, not gated by any actual change), not a guess.
result.verdict: Pending Gene's re-test with the SAME Web Inspector Timelines method on the Experience section specifically this time (correctly targeted). Also pending: Gene reported the page randomly reloading back to the top 1-2 times mid-browse - not yet investigated, asked him for repro details (backgrounding the app/switching tabs first? how long into the session? which section at the time?) since this smells like iOS Safari's memory-pressure tab eviction given how much runs continuously in this hero (WebGL scene + 2D particle canvas), which would be a bigger architectural question (ties to P5's low-end-device fallback idea) rather than a quick fix.

plan.priority: discovered mid-session, not in original P1-P5
plan.name: Round 5: portrait texture resolution, Work glow size, Travel preload margin, then the ACTUAL Experience root cause via a correctly-scoped trace
plan.why: Gene's next test round surfaced four things at once: (1) Work card's outer ambient glow still too prominent visually, (2) skepticism that the portrait DPR revert (P2 follow-up) actually worked, (3) Experience still just as janky, (4) Travel section's globe popping in ~0.5s late when scrolled to. Also two failed attempts at getting a correctly-scoped Web Inspector recording of Experience specifically - first attempt was actually a 2.35s page-LOAD recording (Gene had 'stop recording on page load' checked and reloaded mid-record), second attempt needed Gene walked through deselecting a filtered single-category view to see the full breakdown table again.
plan.how: (1)+(4) were straightforward: Work glow's inset spread and peak opacity reduced further on mobile (kept for later, not root-caused via trace). (2) was a genuine second bug, independent of the P2 DPR-cap revert: the portrait masking canvas in OrbitalSystem.tsx was hardcoded to size=512 regardless of the source photo's actual 900x900 resolution - at the displayed 300 CSS px max size and DPR up to 3, 900 physical px are needed, so 512 was always going to look soft on high-DPR phones, independent of the renderer's own pixelRatio setting. (3) The THIRD correctly-scoped Web Inspector recording (after walking Gene through unchecking 'stop on load' and re-recording specifically on Experience) showed continuous 'Style Invalidation'/'Recalculate Style' for ~9.5s straight, but 'Layout' was comparatively sparse/bursty rather than continuous - a signature of an animation affecting paint/style but not geometry. Traced to the Work filmstrip's accent-ring 'breathing' glow (converted from a Framer JS loop to a CSS @keyframes animation back in WF2, specifically to get it off the main thread) - CSS animations, unlike the Framer/JS-driven rAF loops elsewhere in this codebase, do NOT automatically pause when their element is off-screen or nested under an opacity:0 ancestor. All 11 Work cards' glow animations were running continuously in the background regardless of which section was actually in view, the whole time Gene was testing Experience.

result.implementation: Portrait: masking canvas size changed from hardcoded 512 to Math.min(900, max(image.width, image.height)) - matches the source photo's native resolution. Work glow: inset spread -6%/-8% -> -1%/-2%, peak opacity 0.55 -> 0.28, blur 20px -> 14px, all mobile-only. Travel: DeferredTravelSection's IntersectionObserver rootMargin raised 1500px -> 2800px for more fetch/init lead time on mobile networks (this is a 3rd-party library's - react-globe.gl - own init cost, not something stageable like OrbitalSystem, so this only gives it a head start rather than fixing the underlying cost). Experience root cause: added an IntersectionObserver on the Filmstrip track (same pattern as OrbitalSystem/ParticleNetwork's existing visibility gating) that sets a data-in-view attribute; the breathing-ring's sx gates animation-play-state to 'paused' via a '[data-in-view="false"] &' selector when the whole Work section is out of view. This toggle only fires on scrolling the whole section into/out of view (rare), unlike the earlier backdrop-filter toggle (WF1 follow-up) that fired every scroll frame and made things worse - that lesson directly informed choosing this low-frequency toggle point.
result.verification: Portrait: screenshot crop at 3x DPR confirms sharp detail. Work glow: screenshot confirms visibly tighter/dimmer glow. Experience fix: verified programmatically via Puppeteer that the track's data-in-view attribute and the ring's computed animationPlayState correctly read {inView:false, paused} at Hero and Experience, {inView:true, running} at Work.
result.verdict: Pending Gene's re-test - ideally a 4th Web Inspector recording of Experience to confirm the continuous Style/Recalculate-Style activity is actually gone now, which would be the first fully-confirmed root-cause-to-fix loop in this whole investigation. Two lower-confidence candidates NOT yet touched: HeroSection.tsx has two more always-running CSS animations (a 1s opacity-blink typewriter cursor, a 22s transform-rotate dashed ring) that share the same off-screen-doesn't-pause property as the Work glow did - not gated to Hero's own visibility yet, but both are single elements with cheap properties (opacity toggle, transform rotate is compositor-only) vs. the Work glow's 11 elements with expensive large-blur box-shadows, so lower priority unless a future trace still shows residual continuous style/paint work.

openQuestions: Priority order: P1 (stop the main-thread block) is the clear highest-value fix since it explains the actual regression measured; is Gene fine with P2-P5 being sequenced after, or is there a specific one he wants first?
Is a graceful low-end fallback (P5) worth the added code path complexity, or is 'everyone gets the WebGL scene' an acceptable tradeoff once P1/P2 land and the numbers are re-measured?

Should Work section's StageCard filmstrip (11 cards, each with live useScroll + several motion values, backdrop-filter blur) get a similar look now that Work isn't part of this measurement pass - re-run Lighthouse scrolled/interacted, not just initial load, to see if it's a second hot spot?
